card.title: Oxidation Number and Rules for Assigning It

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: The oxidation number is chemistry's universal charge ledger: a formal value assigned by nine rules — free elements 0, ions their charge, fluorine locked at −1, oxygen −2 (with the peroxide −1, superoxide −½ and OF₂ +2 exceptions), hydrogen +1 (−1 in metal hydrides), and the sum always equal to the species' charge.…

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Check O for peroxides before anything else:** the −1 default-breaker appears in H₂O₂, Na₂O₂, BaO₂ — and in every H₂O₂ redox question.  ·  **Group number caps:** group 1 metals cannot show +2; the maximum positive oxidation number is the group number (Al stops at +3, Mn's ceiling is +7).

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***The +7 summit*** — Mn in KMnO₄ sits at the highest state a 3d element reaches; its fall to +2 in acid (5 electrons) is why permanganate titrations dominate quantitative analysis.

rows.text: **NEB 2024 (3m): State the rules for assigning oxidation numbers. rows.label: Hints
rows.text: Quote at least five rules explicitly before the calculation — the rules carry marks of their own. Show the sum equation with every term, then solve; a bare answer of +7 without the algebra earns half.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Oxidation number is the bridge topic: it detects redox (numbers move), measures extent (n-factor and equivalents), and powers the balancing methods of topic 40 — one bookkeeping system, three jobs.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Nine rules: free 0; ion = charge; F −1 always; O −2 (−1 peroxide, −½ superoxide, +2 in OF₂); H +1 (−1 in metal hydrides); sum = charge; max positive = group number; EN atom negative; fractional averages allowed. Values: Mn/KMnO₄ +7, Cr/K₂Cr₂O₇ +6, S/H₂SO₄ +6, N/HNO₃ +5, Cl/HClO₄ +7, C: CH₄ −4, CO₂ +4.…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: The Mars rover hunts haematite (Fe₂O₃, Fe +3) because iron's oxidation states record a planet's water history — oxidation numbers as geological fingerprints.

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: **NEB-style (2m): Using oxidation numbers, identify what is oxidised and what is reduced in 2KI + Cl₂ → 2KCl + I₂.** — Iodine moves from **−1** (in KI) to **0** (in I₂): its oxidation number increases, so iodide is **oxidised** and acts as the reducing agent.…

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — The Charge Ledger of Every Atom The oxidation number is a formal charge — the value an atom would carry if every bond were fully ionic. It is not a physical charge, but it is the most useful fiction in chemistry: it tracks electron control through any reaction, flags the redox pair in an instant, and supplies the balancing engine of topic 40.…  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts ### 2.1 The rules (in checking order) 1. **Free element = 0:** O₂, H₂, Fe, S₈, P₄ — all zero. 2. **Monatomic ion = its charge:** Na⁺ +1, Ca²⁺ +2, Cl⁻ −1, Al³⁺ +3. 3. **Fluorine = −1 always** — the only element with no exceptions (even in OF₂ it stays −1, forcing O to +2). 4.…  ·  ## 3. Scientific Definitions | Term | Scientific meaning | Example | |---|---|---| | **Oxidation number** | Formal charge if all bonds were ionic | Mn = +7 in KMnO₄ | | **Oxidation** | Increase in oxidation number | Fe²⁺ → Fe³⁺ | | **Reduction** | Decrease in oxidation number | Mn +7 → +2 | | **n-factor** | Electrons transferred per formula unit | K₂Cr₂O₇ n = 6 | |…

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ## 6. Common Confusions **Oxidation number ≠ ionic charge:** Mn(+7) in KMnO₄ is bookkeeping; there is no free Mn⁷⁺ ion. Charges belong to actual ions; numbers belong to atoms inside any species.  ·  **The peroxide exception is the favourite exam trap:** defaulting O to −2 in H₂O₂ wrecks the sum — check for O–O bonds first.  ·  **Fractional answers are correct answers:** +8/3 and +2.5 are legitimate averages; do not "fix" them into integers.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ## 7. Exam Application **Verified PYQ (NEB 2024): State the rules for assigning oxidation numbers. Find the oxidation number of Mn in KMnO₄ and Cr in K₂Cr₂O₇.** — Rules: (1) free elements 0; (2) monatomic ions equal their charges; (3) fluorine −1 in all compounds; (4) oxygen −2 except −1 in peroxides and +2 in OF₂;…  ·  **NEB-style (2m): Find the oxidation number of S in Na₂S₄O₆ and Fe in Fe₃O₄.** — **Tetrathionate:** 2(+1) + 4S + 6(−2) = 0 → 4S = +10 → S = **+2.5** (an average: two S at 0, two at +5). **Magnetite:** 3Fe + 4(−2) = 0 → Fe = **+8/3** (FeO·Fe₂O₃: one +2, two +3).  ·  **NEB-style (2m): Identify the redox pair in 2KI + Cl₂ → 2KCl + I₂.** — Iodine: −1 in KI → 0 in I₂ (increase — oxidised; Cl₂ is the oxidising agent). Chlorine: 0 → −1 (decrease — reduced; I⁻ is the reducing agent). K⁺ and the chloride counterions are spectators at +1 throughout.
